summary: Kootenai NF lookout near Troy, MT: 1924 platform tower and cabin (cabin still stands), 1934 pole tower, 1963 53-ft R-6 tower; access closed for grizzly habitat, 2026 reactivation assessment.

facts.design: Treated-timber 53-ft R-6 tower with flat cab (1963), third lookout on the site; earlier 1934 50-ft L-4 pole tower and 1924 50-ft platform tower with cabin

access.note: The access road and area are closed to protect grizzly bear habitat; the closure was still in place in the 2026 condition assessment.

visit.trail_note: Access closed for grizzly bear habitat; firelookout.com says the tower is available for emergencies

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: First structures: a 50-ft platform tower and a log cabin; the cabin still stands
A 50-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab followed; its foundation stones remain
Present 53-ft treated-timber R-6 tower, the third lookout on the site
Date registered per NHLR detail page: August 30, 2015

Condition assessment with the Forest Service ahead of the 2026 fire season; exploring reactivation as a staffed fire lookout; upgrading lightning protection is a top priority for the Forest Service and volunteers
Access to the area currently closed off to protect grizzly bear habitat (start date not stated)

corrections.why: The record's 15.2 m is 50 ft, the height of the 1934 pole tower. All three sources describe the present tower as 53 ft, which is about 16.2 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 3,783 ft (1,153 m), matching the record's elevation_m 1153.1. firelookout.com gives 4943 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure, and the story gives no elevation.

notes_for_editor: The brief says the NHLR record shares a register number with another entry (US 1114, MT 62). Check for a duplicate record. Elevation conflicts (3,783 ft in NHLR vs 4943 ft on firelookout.com), and the record keeps the NHLR figure. Height correction: 15.2 m is 50 ft, the 1934 tower's height; the present 53-ft tower is about 16.2 m. The firelookout.com page is undated and says the tower is available for emergencies; the 2026 assessment says current access is closed for grizzly habitat. Do not encourage visiting. The 2026 condition assessment PDF linked from the NWMT page was not opened.
